lines.en: Thank you for calling Bright Net. This is Amy. How can I help you?
lines.pt: Obrigada por ligar para a Bright Net. Aqui é a Amy. Como posso ajudar?

lines.en: Hi, Amy. **I’m following up on** a problem I reported on Monday. My reference number is R-2086.
lines.pt: Oi, Amy. Estou fazendo um acompanhamento de um problema que relatei na segunda. Meu número de referência é R-2086.

lines.en: Thanks. **Let me check** that. Could you hold on for a moment?
lines.pt: Obrigada. Vou verificar. Você poderia aguardar um momento?

lines.en: Of course. **As I mentioned** on Monday, my internet still doesn’t work in my new apartment.
lines.pt: Claro. Como mencionei na segunda, minha internet ainda não funciona no meu novo apartamento.

lines.en: Thanks for your patience. I see your case. A technician was supposed to visit yesterday, but the visit was canceled.
lines.pt: Obrigada pela paciência. Vejo o seu caso. Um técnico deveria visitar ontem, mas a visita foi cancelada.

lines.en: I’m afraid that’s a problem. I work from home. **Could you confirm** a new appointment, please?
lines.pt: Receio que isso seja um problema. Trabalho de casa. Você poderia confirmar uma nova visita, por favor?

lines.en: Yes. I can schedule a technician for Thursday morning, between eight and noon.
lines.pt: Sim. Posso agendar um técnico para quinta de manhã, entre oito e meio-dia.

lines.en: Thursday works. **In the meantime**, could I get a temporary hotspot?
lines.pt: Quinta funciona. Enquanto isso, eu poderia receber um ponto de acesso temporário?

lines.en: I can send one today. You’ll receive an email with all the details in a few minutes.
lines.pt: Posso enviar um hoje. Você receberá um e-mail com todos os detalhes em alguns minutos.

lines.en: Perfect. Thank you for your help, Amy. I really appreciate it.
lines.pt: Perfeito. Obrigada pela ajuda, Amy. Eu agradeço muito.

pages.title: Real-Life Mission Day 11

situation.text: Ida has had a bad week: a faulty router she bought, no internet in her new apartment, a noisy neighbor and a lost bag. Today she chains calls, visits and messages to fix everything, and you play her team.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can chain the situations of the unit: explain a problem, complain politely, ask for help, follow up and confirm a solution, in one connected mission.

Complain or ask for a change politely with Could you…?

Confirm the solution and the next step
success: I ask politely for a solution.
I follow up on an earlier request.
I confirm the next step and thank the person.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Following Up in the USA
pages.intro: When a problem is not solved on the first try, Americans often follow up. Look at the cards and guess how to do it politely.

cards.note: A ticket or reference number lets you say exactly which problem you mean when you call or write again.
If the agent cannot help, it is normal to ask politely: “Could I speak to a supervisor?”
Many people ask: “When can I expect a response?” It is polite, specific and keeps the case moving.

qs.q: Why is a reference number useful when you follow up?
qs.pt: Por que o número de referência ajuda no follow-up?

levels.A2: It helps the agent find my case quickly.
levels.B1: It identifies the earlier request, so you do not have to explain everything again.
levels.B2: It lets any agent see the full history of the case, saving time and avoiding repetition.

qs.q: When can you ask for a supervisor?
qs.pt: Quando você pode pedir um supervisor?

levels.A2: When the agent cannot solve the problem.
levels.B1: Politely, if the issue stays unresolved after you have explained it clearly.
levels.B2: As a reasonable next step once the standard channel has not led to a solution.

qs.q: How can you stay polite but firm?

levels.A2: Use Could you…? and say what you need.
levels.B1: State the problem and the date clearly, and ask for a specific next step.
levels.B2: Combine courteous phrasing with concrete facts and a clear request, such as a deadline.

pages.compare: In Brazil, people often call again and again or turn to a consumer agency after a failed attempt. In the USA, it is common to keep a reference number, follow up in writing and ask politely for a supervisor first. What works where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e levantar hipóteses antes do diálogo.

extra: Do people follow up in writing in your country?

support: Use as respostas do nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam em voz alta.
stretch: B2: compare convenções de cortesia no atendimento no Brasil e nos EUA.

swap.frame: I’m following up on my {topic}. Could you confirm {detail}?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I’m following up on my request.
I am writing to follow up on my previous request.
As I mentioned, it’s still not fixed.
As previously stated, the issue remains unresolved.
Please confirm the date at your earliest convenience.
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules: contractions also appear in informal writing.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: To be clear and firm, stress the key information, not every word: “My reference number is R-twenty-oh-EIGHT-six”. Keep your tone calm and slightly slower for dates, times and numbers.

items.say: I’m following up on Monday’s request.
items.linked: I’m FOL·lowing UP on MON·day’s re·QUEST.

own.prompt: Write one sentence with a day and a time that you want someone to confirm.
own.criteria: Say it twice: first at normal speed, then with stress on the day and the time. Is the key information clear?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: sentence stress for clarity.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e entonação → usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e em velocidade normal; peça que o estudante bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria usando o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: I’m following up on Monday. · Could you confirm the time?

errors.r: acento na informação-chave: dia e hora

pages.title: Group mission — fix the whole week
pages.goal: Real-Life Mission Day: each group chains three situations of the unit in a row, keeping a polite tone from start to finish.

missions.mission: Chain: (1) return the faulty router at the store, (2) call the internet company about the outage, (3) follow up on Thursday’s visit.
missions.constraint: Use “I’d like to return…”, “I’m calling about…” and “I’m following up on…”.

missions.mission: Chain: (1) tell the neighbor the music is too loud, (2) ask the building manager for the quiet hours, (3) confirm the solution in writing.
missions.constraint: Use “Could you keep it down?” and “Could you confirm…?”.

missions.mission: Chain: (1) report a lost bag at the station, (2) fix a wrong dish at a restaurant, (3) call the company to confirm a new appointment.
missions.constraint: Use “I’ve lost my…”, “This isn’t what I ordered” and “In the meantime…”.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short follow-up email: remind the company of an earlier problem and ask for a clear next step.
pages.model: Hello! **I’m following up on** my request R-2086 from Monday. **As I mentioned**, my internet still doesn’t work. **Could you confirm** the technician’s visit on Thursday? **In the meantime**, could you send a temporary hotspot? Thank you for your help!
checklist: I greeted and gave my reference number.
I asked for a clear next step.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Short words with a clear need.

ladder.say: I’m following up on my request. It still doesn’t work.
ladder.goal: Follow up and say the problem.

ladder.say: I called on Monday, and the technician never came. Could you confirm a new appointment?
This is the second time the visit has been canceled, so I’d appreciate a firm date and a temporary solution.
I appreciate your patience, but given the repeated delays, I’d like this escalated to a supervisor.
I’d be most grateful if this could be addressed without further delay, as it affects my work considerably.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está (A2) e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
